figure: export/buy-back rate Rs 10.00-11.30/kWh and the Rs 11.0 benchmark
claimed: Rs. 10.00 - 11.30 per kWh with benchmark Rs. 11.0/kWh, determined by National Average Energy Purchase Price (NAEPP / EPP) / avoided variable fuel generation cost.
actual: S.R.O. 251(I)/2026 Regulation 14(1)(b) establishes a floating rate tied to the 'national average energy purchase price' (NAEPP), not a static rate of Rs. 10.00-11.30 or Rs. 11.0. In NEPRA's CY 2026 Power Purchase Price determination (TRF-100/CPPAG dated 2026-01-07), NAEPP is determined as Rs. 8.13/kWh (NAPPP is Rs. 25.32/kWh). The Rs. 10.00-11.30 range reflects secondary market estimates and FY 2024-25 historical averages.
clause: Regulation 14(1)(b): 'the kWh supplied by prosumer to the licensee, shall be billed in accordance with the national average energy purchase price.' Explanation: ''net billing arrangement' means an arrangement under which electricity generated by distributed generation facility of prosumer is purchased by the licensee and the licensee raises the bill on the prosumer for his consumption at the applicable tariff, after giving credit for electricity supplied by prosumer to the licensee at the national average energy purchase price.' TRF-100 Decision Para 36: 'the National Average Energy Purchase Price (NAEPP) works out as Rs.8.13/kWh.'

figure: net billing vs net metering mechanism
claimed: Net Billing mechanism replacing 1:1 volumetric net metering; grid imports billed at standard retail slab tariff, surplus grid exports credited separately at buyback rate; net monetary balance billed/credited; self-consumption behind the meter retained.
actual: Net billing regime enacted under Regulation 14(1) decoupling imports and exports. Imports are billed at applicable consumer retail tariff; surplus exports are credited at the national average energy purchase price. Volumetric 1:1 netting under repealed 2015 regulations (Regulation 14 of S.R.O. 812(I)/2015) is eliminated for new connections.
clause: Regulation 14(1): 'At the end of each billing cycle, following the date of interconnection of distributed generation facility to its distribution system, the licensee shall raise its bill after taking into account the electricity generated and consumed by the prosumer under a net billing arrangement as follows: (a) the kWh supplied by licensee to prosumer, shall be billed in accordance with the applicable tariff. (b) the kWh supplied by prosumer to the licensee, shall be billed in accordance with the national average energy purchase price.'

claimed: Monthly billing cycle; surplus monetary export credit carries forward to offset subsequent monthly electricity bills.
actual: Settlement is calculated on a 30-day billing cycle. Any surplus credit carries forward against the prosumer's subsequent billing cycle or is paid out quarterly by the distribution licensee.
clause: Regulation 2(1)(viii): ''billing cycle' means energy recorded by the meters in a period of thirty days;' Regulation 14(2): 'In case the billed amount of the kWh supplied by prosumer exceeds the billed amount of kWh supplied by licensee, the net billed amount shall be credited against prosumer's next billing cycle or shall be paid by the licensee to the prosumer quarterly.'

figure: system size limit: 100% of sanctioned load
claimed: Distributed generation facility capacity cannot exceed 100% of the consumer's sanctioned load.
actual: System capacity is strictly restricted to not exceed the sanctioned load of the consumer premises.
clause: Regulation 3(2): 'The capacity of a proposed distributed generation facility shall not exceed the sanctioned load of the applicant's premises: Provided that the Authority may revise the capacity of proposed distributed generation facility at any time through a notification.'

claimed: Cumulative distributed generation capacity connected to a distribution transformer capped at 80% of its rated capacity.
actual: Distribution licensee is legally prohibited from entertaining any application once connected distributed generation capacity reaches 80% of the distribution transformer's rated capacity.
clause: Regulation 3(5) second proviso: 'Provided further that the licensee shall not entertain any application if the distributed generation capacity connected to a particular distribution transformer has reached 80% of its rated capacity.'

claimed: Distributed generation facilities <= 25 kW exempt from direct NEPRA concurrence requirement; approved directly by DISCO.
actual: Prosumers installing distributed generation facilities of 25 kW or below are explicitly exempted from seeking NEPRA concurrence; the concerned licensee accords direct approval.
clause: S.R.O. 1330(I)/2026 Section 2 (inserting second proviso to Regulation 4(1)): 'Provided that a prosumer having distributed generation facility of 25 kW or below capacity shall not be required to seek concurrence from the Authority and the concerned licensee shall accord its approval.'

claimed: Maximum distributed generation facility capacity capped at 1 MW (1,000 kW).
actual: Regulations apply to distributed generation facilities from 1 kW up to a maximum cap of 1 MW (1,000 kW).
clause: Regulation 2(1)(ix): ''distributed generation facility' or 'DG facility' means a facility set up by a prosumer using solar, wind or biogas energy resource for generation of electricity up to 1 MW;' Schedule-I Heading: 'Distributed Generation Interconnection Agreement (1 kW to 1MW)'

figure: system size limit: 250 kW load flow study threshold
claimed: Mandatory load flow study for distributed generation systems >= 250 kW.
actual: A load flow study conducted through the licensee or a PEC-registered consultant is legally mandatory for installations with capacity of 250 kW or above.
clause: Regulation 3(3): 'An applicant proposing to install a distributed generation facility with an installed capacity of 250 kW or above shall be obligated to conduct and submit a load flow study carried out through the licensee or any reputable consultant registered with Pakistan Engineering Council.'

figure: DISCO fees for LESCO: NEPRA concurrence fee
claimed: NEPRA concurrence fee of PKR 1,000 per kW for systems > 25 kW; Nil (PKR 0) for systems <= 25 kW.
actual: One-time concurrence application fee of Rs. 1,000/kW payable to NEPRA under Schedule-IV; systems <= 25 kW are exempted from concurrence under S.R.O. 1330(I)/2026, making the fee PKR 0.
clause: Schedule-IV [Regulation 4(2)(b)]: 'An application for concurrence shall be accompanied with one-time fee of one thousand rupees per kilowatt (Rs. 1000/kW) or as may be notified from time to time, paid in favour of National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (NEPRA).' S.R.O. 1330(I)/2026 Section 2: Prosumers <= 25 kW 'shall not be required to seek concurrence from the Authority'.

figure: DISCO fees for LESCO: processing fee, meter cost, liaison fee
claimed: DISCO processing fee PKR 15,000-25,000; bidirectional meter & testing PKR 35,000-75,000; turnkey EPC liaison PKR 70,000-110,000.
actual: Primary regulations do not legislate fixed national tariff ranges like Rs 15,000-25,000 or Rs 35,000-75,000. Under Regulation 3(9) and Regulation 12(1), DISCOs recover costs via site-specific Connection Charge Estimates / Demand Notices based on actual metering and interconnection equipment costs. Turnkey liaison fees are private market transactions not governed by statutory notifications.
clause: Regulation 3(9): 'Within seven working days of execution of the agreement, the licensee shall issue the connection charge estimate to the prosumer for the proposed interconnection facility up to the interconnection point including the metering installation.' Regulation 12(1): 'Prosumer shall be responsible for all costs associated with interconnection facilities up to the interconnection point including metering installation.'

claimed: Valid until the expiration of the original agreement tenure (standard 7 years from agreement date); retains 1:1 volumetric net metering; material modification forfeits protection.
actual: S.R.O. 547(I)/2026 protects legacy net-metered generators 'till the expiry of the term of such agreement' without specifying a '7-year term'. Under the repealed 2015 regulations (S.R.O. 812(I)/2015, Regulation 7(1)), the statutory agreement term was 3 years, renewable. Under 2026 regulations (Regulation 7(1)), the agreement term is 5 years. The 7-year figure is an administrative licensing convention or secondary market assumption, not a statutory contract term. The forfeiture upon material modification is confirmed.
clause: S.R.O. 547(I)/2026 Section 1 (substituting Regulation 21(2)): '(2) Notwithstanding the repeal effected by these regulations, nothing shall affect approvals granted, licences or concurrences issued, and agreements executed under the repealed regulations before the commencement of these regulations, and any distributed generator having a valid agreement executed under the repealed regulations shall be billed in accordance with the rate and mechanism provided in the repealed regulations till the expiry of the term of such agreement: Provided that the savings to the distributed generator with regard to rate and billing mechanism during the currency of existing agreement shall cease to be applicable in case of material modification of distributed generation facility resulting in change to the maximum electrical output of the distributed generation facility of the distributed generator having a licence or concurrence or approval granted under the repealed regulations.' S.R.O. 812(I)/2015 Regulation 7(1): 'The term of the Agreement between Distributed Generator and Distribution Company shall be three years with effect from commissioning of Distributed Generator Facility.'
